_doc: Key-statement readers (coarse-graining skill): two independent readers label every candidate of a batch (main,
key, technical, bookkeeping) and write one sentence each; their printed tables go to kappa.py. Units are the
batches written by inventory.py --candidates: paste its batches.json over the example units below, and set
'batches' to its output directory. One review stage, two reviews: reader-a and reader-b, each with its own
profile, on the same frozen packet (the batch file). Driver: rollout.py of the writing-workflow skill (field table
Families: rollout.py compares a reviewer's family only with the writer of a preceding write stage. This config
has none, so the driver does not check the readers' families: choose them here. Two families (here the profiles
reader-claude and reader-gpt) reduce shared blind spots; two runs of one model measure the consistency of one
procedure (the Yang-Mills readers were two runs of one model). Say which you did when you publish kappa. If you
add a write stage before 'read' and a reader shares the writer's family, the stage needs "allow_same_family": true.
The codex profile assumes that 'codex exec' prints only the agent's final message on standard output; check it
with your version (agent_cli.py --preflight), and remove banner lines with strip_lines if needed.
After the run: kappa.py --a WORKDIR/*/read/reader-a.md --b WORKDIR/*/read/reader-b.md
Use: replace every SET-ME value, run rollout.py rollout.key-statements.example.json --dry-run, then without
--dry-run; try one batch first (--only B001). The two units below are placeholders in the format of batches.json.
workdir: SET-ME: working directory for the readers (outside the skills repository)

reader-claude._doc: Claude Code in print mode with read-only tools (as the reviewer profile of writing-workflow's agents.example.json).

reader-gpt._doc: Codex CLI in its read-only sandbox; it reads anywhere and writes nowhere.

vars.project: SET-ME: one line naming the formal result, e.g. OpenAI's Lean proof of the construction of four-dimensional quantum Yang-Mills theory
vars.lean_root: SET-ME: the Lean source checked out at the pinned commit (read-only)
vars.map: SET-ME: the map directory: statement.md (the statement page of phase 0), units.tsv
vars.batches: SET-ME: the output directory of inventory.py --candidates (B001.md, ..., candidates.tsv)

B001.title: unit U1 (title of the unit), candidates 1-20 of 40

B002.title: unit U1 (title of the unit), candidates 21-40 of 40
